lede: The biggest thing on the docket this week is the Carhenge redevelopment, which lands before two separate bodies on September 30 — HARC reviews the preliminary architecture for the multi-building project at 700 W. Pacific, while a special Town Council session takes up the appeal of the lot-subdivision approval that has to happen before any of it can move forward. Alongside that, the Gondola Leadership Committee makes a consequential choice between federal funding and local project delivery, and the County Commissioners dig into a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee.

notable.stake: Council votes on federal vs. local delivery for gondola — shapes financing and control.
HARC reviews preliminary architecture for all Carhenge building clusters at 700 W. Pacific.
Council hears appeal of P&Z's Carhenge lot-subdivision approval — could halt redevelopment.
Commissioners workshop a new Employee Housing Impact Fee for unincorporated San Miguel County.
Final architecture review for 15 employee apartments and four new multifamily units in Mountain Village.
2027 General Fund and Capital budget contours take shape before formal adoption begins.
